task: Find a FREE sub-hourly historical surface-obs feed for SBGR (Sao Paulo-Guarulhos), the exact station Polymarket's Sao Paulo high-temp ladder settles on (per ref/pmkt_settlement_basis.md row: '...Sao Paulo-Guarulhos International Airport Station...' wunderground.com/history/daily/br/guarulhos/SBGR, network BR__ASOS confirmed present, basis SOUND with 14/14 IEM-vs-settlement agreement).
verdict_tier: No sub-hourly (or even reliably-finer-than-hourly) free feed found for SBGR or any station genuinely co-located with Guarulhos airport. Every candidate checked either (a) only republishes the same hourly-plus-irregular-special METAR SBGR itself issues, or (b) is a real automatic-station network with a finer nominal cadence but has NO station at/near the airport site (so it would not carry the settlement basis). This negative result is reported plainly per GROUNDING.md non-negotiable #9.
headline: SBGR's own surface obs are METAR/SPECI, confirmed HOURLY-ONLY as the routine cadence: DECEA's own help documentation states verbatim 'Os dados das estacoes meteorologicas de superficie dos aeroportos (Metar) sao coletados de uma em uma hora ou em horarios intermediarios caso esteja ocorrendo algum evento especial' (collected hour-by-hour, or at intermediate times only if a special event is occurring). Verified with a real 51-day IEM ASOS pull (2026-06-01 to 2026-07-22): 1284 rows over 51 days = 24.2 rows/day average; 1224/1284 (95.3%) fall exactly on minute :00, and the remaining ~60 irregular-minute rows are sparse, non-periodic SPECI (weather-triggered, not a fixed sub-hourly schedule) averaging ~1.2/day -- nowhere close to the >=100 rows/day sub-hourly proof bar, and structurally different from EGLC/RJTT's clean twice-hourly :20/:50 SPECI pattern found in the prior London/Tokyo feedhunts. Checked INMET (Brazil's national met agency): automatic-station data is explicitly hourly-only per INMET's own documentation ('disponibilizados diariamente, de hora em hora'), AND INMET has no automatic station at Guarulhos airport -- the nearest is A701 Sao Paulo-Mirante, 16.4km away (a materially different site, unlike Tokyo's ~0.3km-away co-located JMA AMeDAS point), so it would fail the settlement-basis-match requirement even if it were sub-hourly. Checked REDEMET (DECEA's aviation met network/API): its only public product is METAR/SPECI messages (API-gated, requires free registration) -- same underlying hourly+special cadence as SBGR's own METAR, confirmed via DECEA's help docs describing even their 'meteograma' graphing tool as a visualization of METAR/TAF, not a separate finer-cadence source. Checked CGE-SP (Sao Paulo city's Centro de Gerenciamento de Emergencias, which does run a genuine 5-10min automatic-station network): pulled the live station list (32 stations) -- none are at Guarulhos (a separate municipality bordering, but outside, the city of Sao Paulo); nearest CGE stations are ~10+km away in Sao Paulo's eastern zone (Penha, Sao Miguel Paulista, Vila Maria/Guilherme), not co-located with SBGR. Infraero's 2013 'updated every 5 minutes' airport weather page was a UI refresh of the same METAR-derived status (green/yellow/red operational indicator), not a new observation source, and its current-availability/historical-archive status is unverified/likely defunct (2013 news article, no API found). Open-Meteo historical is model reanalysis, excluded per task rule. Meteostat's bulk historical is hourly-resampled, excluded (would not beat the METAR baseline anyway). MADIS and Synoptic Data free tier were not independently pulled (registration/token-gated in this session) but are exceptionally unlikely to beat this result: both aggregate FROM national feeds via GTS/METAR relay for a country like Brazil where no genuine sub-hourly national station feed at this airport was found to exist in the first place -- there is no finer upstream source for them to carry. OGIMET returned a bot-block page for both its SYNOP and METAR display endpoints in this session (confirmed via direct pull, same blocked-page byte size as seen in the prior London feedhunt's cache) and would in any case only mirror the same SBGR METAR already characterized via IEM.

auth_summary: The (non-viable) baseline METAR feeds (IEM, aviationweather.gov) require no auth. INMET's station catalog requires no auth but needs a browser-like User-Agent header (bare curl gets a TLS connection reset). REDEMET's API, MADIS, and Synoptic Data all require free account/token registration, not completed this session since none was expected to clear the sub-hourly bar given what was independently confirmed about the underlying station cadence.
rate_limits_summary: No hard rate limits encountered on IEM, aviationweather.gov, INMET, or CGE-SP in this session (sequential pulls, ~1/sec with pauses). OGIMET returned bot-block pages regardless of pacing.
licensing_summary: IEM/NOAA METAR mirrors: public domain / free US-government-adjacent reuse. INMET data: Brazilian federal open-data (INMET states its data is public/free for the automatic-station network, per its portal). CGE-SP: Sao Paulo municipal open data, publicly viewable, no explicit license text found in the pages fetched this session -- not relevant here since CGE-SP was excluded on geographic grounds, not licensing.
relevance_to_grounding_blocker: This result CONFIRMS, with fresh real pulls, the exact blocker already named in ref/pmkt_final_verdict.md and GROUNDING.md: 'hourly METAR (only free feed for the 5 non-US cities) under-reports the diurnal peak by ~1h of temperature change' -- for Sao Paulo specifically, unlike the prior London and Tokyo feedhunts (both of which found a genuinely finer free feed: EGLC's native 30-min SPECI cadence and JMA's 10-min AMeDAS respectively), NO finer free feed exists for SBGR or any genuinely co-located station. The GROUNDING GO-path #2 ('a genuinely finer free feed for the international cities from their national met agencies') does NOT pan out for Sao Paulo: INMET (Brazil's national met agency) is itself hourly-only and geographically absent from the airport, and the one genuine sub-hourly Brazilian network found (CGE-SP, city of Sao Paulo) has no coverage of Guarulhos at all. Sao Paulo therefore remains coverage-blocked on this specific mechanism; this is a valid negative finding, not a partial result requiring more digging within the FREE-feed constraint set by this task (the remaining unexplored paths -- REDEMET API, MADIS, Synoptic -- are all gated AND structurally incapable of exceeding the cadence already directly measured at the source, per the reasoning given in each candidate's entry above).
